items.note: University students programmed robot controllers with or without Copilot; code similarity (framed as creativity/structural diversity) and robustness compared; full text shows 13 students split 7/6 by balancing on DAT scores, not random, so it fails the 50-person threshold.

Pre-registered online study where participants post-edit LLM drafts and also write unassisted control texts; embedding-based style similarity shows reduced stylistic diversity versus unassisted text; within-person design, order randomization not stated.

414 participants co-wrote stories with no suggestions or with pro-/anti-stereotypical single-word LM predictive text; the outcome is the stereotype content of stories, not creativity or diversity (same study as arXiv 2409.20390).

Expert interviews followed by an egg-task design experiment comparing ideation with and without GenAI tools; GenAI raised idea counts and supported exploration but did not prevent fixation; N and assignment not in abstract.

Field experiment with 99 knowledge workers at a multinational firm; outputs with GenAI support were more homogeneous in style and content than without across three knowledge-work tasks; assignment method not stated in abstract (abstract from AIS eLibrary page).

Co-creative story writing with a dissenting versus a conforming AI (ai_design contrast); more creative output with the dissenting AI but not significant (p = 0.111); abstract text seen only via researchr/search snippet, N not stated (an ICCC short paper, likely small; a Leiden thesis by Bouter may hold details).

Undergraduates ideated in two workshops, ChatGPT-assisted (n=22) versus analogue (n=17); fluency, flexibility, and originality of ideas scored; assignment is by workshop and likely non-random, below the 50 threshold; follow-up to c724.

Pilot with 35 BYU undergraduates in two workshops, ChatGPT-assisted versus analogue team ideation; fluency, flexibility, originality scored; workshop-level assignment, below the 50 threshold; earlier study by the same team as c723.

DesignAID tool paper: 87 crowd designers compared LLM-to-image generation (low vs high diversity) with Pinterest search, but outcomes are designers' ratings of inspiration, enjoyment, and usefulness of the tool, not scores on their output; Rick et al. (2025) reanalysis of the same users may be relevant.

Randomized experiment with 976 managers comparing an agentic multi-agent AI (Aristotle), general GPT-4o, and no AI on building strategic theories; quality of the theories rated (idea-quality outcome, creativity not named), check whether the task counts as ideation.
